question: what happens when a declared ceiling first binds on real data
block: second repeat of the confirmation block, 8 episodes, giving 16 in total across two repeats

selection_hazard.observation: the only refusal fell in the full condition, which is the condition that uses the most calls in every observation
selection_hazard.consequence: a ceiling that binds asymmetrically removes episodes non-randomly, so simply dropping them would bias any comparison toward the cheaper condition
selection_hazard.second_consequence: the admissible set is now unbalanced at 7 against 8, and the variance guard refuses to compute components on it, which is the correct behaviour rather than a failure

decision_taken: a ceiling violation is treated as an outcome, not as data loss: the episode failed to complete within the declared budget, and the refusal rate per condition is part of what the design reports
why: if the full condition requires more calls, then capping calls is the budget match rather than an accident of instrumentation, and the endpoint becomes completion within budget
not_done: the ceiling was not raised to make the refusal disappear, which would have hidden the very asymmetry the measurement revealed

guard_behaviour.unbalanced_admissible_set: raised, expected mean squares do not apply

claim_scope: admission and selection evidence only; no treatment effect is claimed
